bijection_prior.computation: the count is a permanent of the 0/1 allowance matrix (subset DP); support membership needs only EXISTENCE of a bijection, computed by matching

bijection_prior.posterior: P*(h|E) = #{sigma bijective : (h,sigma) satisfies E} / sum_h' #{sigma bijective : (h',sigma) satisfies E}
bijection_prior.statement: The world declares a set of DISTINCT property vectors; the assignment sigma from symbols to that set is a BIJECTION, unknown to the agent. The prior is uniform over pairs (h, sigma) with sigma bijective: P(h, sigma) proportional to 1.
bijection_prior.why_required: The first implementation assumed conditional independence, W(h)=prod_x n_x(h). That is a DIFFERENT prior which admits every symbol sharing one vector; identification is then impossible and no robust guarantee exists at any depth, i.e. B1 would be unrunnable. The bijection is declared to the agent in phase zero: it is world structure, not hidden law.

clarifications.C1_posterior_is_normative_reference_not_: P*(h|E) is the NORMATIVE PREREGISTERED reference under the declared uniform-bijection prior P(h,sigma) proportional to 1. It is not 'the only rational belief' and not physical ground truth. A deviation (e.g. the Pilot-A 2006-type non-uniform weighting) is a DEVIATION FROM THE PREREGISTERED REFERENCE, not 'absolutely wrong belief'. An agent that declares a different prior before the session is judged as a different policy, not as an error. The frozen reference exists so measurements are comparable, not to deny alternative priors.
clarifications.C2_permanent_tractability_limit: The exact reference posterior counts consistent bijections = the permanent of a 0/1 matrix, which is #P-hard in general. Exact computation is tractable ONLY at the current small-world scale (n_train ~6). Scaling B1 requires approximation of the permanent or a differently-structured latent-assignment family. Recorded as a known limit; NOT solved now.
clarifications.C3_ig_law_of_probe_operational_not_liter: A-005's invariant 'IG_law(PROBE)=0' is OPERATIONALLY correct — probing ALONE never discriminates laws (verified by the probe-free adversarial bot that cannot reach the blind criterion). It is NOT literally true post-experiment: a PROBE on a symbol whose EXPERIMENT was already observed can have IG_law > 0, because it completes the H<->Sigma coupling. Empirically found in the B1-small audit (seed 4006, action P:Kr: IG_H=1.0 with negative interaction = redundancy). The PRESERVED invariant is the operational one; the literal marginal statement is hereby corrected.

corrected_definition.separation_recorded: World-instance unreachable != Epistemically knowable as unreachable. Only the second is ever used for scoring.
wrong_in_two_ways: clairvoyant: that floor is known only after the truth is known

weak criterion: it scores the vote against the TRUE law, whereas what an agent can guarantee is agreement against EVERY surviving hypothesis. Measured on world 3000 the two read 2 versus 6 and are not comparable quantities — the weak/strict bifurcation of A-004 resurfacing.

decision_states.GUARANTEED_REACHABLE: every branch can be driven to the criterion within B -> CONTINUE
decision_states.MET: the criterion already holds -> correct decision: STOP/SUFFICIENCY
decision_states.POSSIBLE_UNGUARANTEED: D_lower <= B < D_robust: a lucky branch reaches it, no policy guarantees it -> RECORDED, NOT SCORED as correct or incorrect
decision_states.UNREACHABLE: B < D_lower(belief): not even the luckiest consistent branch reaches it -> INCOMPLETE
decision_states.derivation: ALL FOUR are computed from the BELIEF STATE (evidence + surviving support), never from W*. The project rule holds: we do not judge an agent against information it has no access to.

payload.frozen: grammar, schema, world, the four rulers, tau_ID and the audit rule are unchanged. The single controlled variable is the DECLARED BUDGET; the agent is told it, as always.
payload.generation: stratified deliberately, not by shrinking the budget at random. UNREACHABLE is produced by setting the declared budget B < D_lower(belief_0) — a quantity the agent can itself compute from the catalogue and its evidence, so the verdict it is judged by is one it could in principle reach.

measurement_unit.clustering: episode/world, per appendix C.3, to prevent pseudo-replication. No test may treat N steps from M worlds as N independent observations; confirmatory analysis is cluster-aware or summarises per world first.
measurement_unit.unit: DECISION POINT (at every step the agent faces stop / continue / declare incomplete)

payload.next_step_rule: no training after this. First identify WHICH CELL of the control policy fails, so the training target is specific instead of a vague 'be more efficient'.
payload.preregistered_expectation: if the agent is strong on MET and GUARANTEED_REACHABLE but keeps going under UNREACHABLE until the budget runs out, then the deficit is NOT action exhaustion as first supposed, but an inability to establish the LIMITS OF ITS FUTURE KNOWLEDGE: 'I do not know' != 'I know that I cannot know within this budget'. That would be a strong result in itself.
payload.primary_output: CONFUSION MATRIX over scored decision points, NOT an episode success rate.

secondary_metric.ControlDecisionAccuracy: correct scored decisions / scored decision points
secondary_metric.explicit_caveat: must NOT be read alone: with unbalanced classes a high accuracy can conceal total failure on UNREACHABLE. The matrix governs.

payload.title: Epistemic control diagnostic: four belief-derived decision states, scored per decision point
payload.why_the_middle_band_is_not_scored: the ambiguity is not in the world but in a DECISION RULE we have not yet fixed: continuing is rational under expected value, stopping is rational under a robust-only rule. Scoring it would punish reasonable behaviour. It is analysed separately, where it may later reveal the agent's risk attitude.

1_non_finite_probabilities.now: every probability must be a finite real in [0,1]; bool rejected; the sum is checked only after each value passes. _canon uses allow_nan=False so a non-finite value can never enter a sealed record.
1_non_finite_probabilities.was: only the SUM was checked: abs(nan - 1.0) > 1e-6 evaluates to False, so a distribution containing NaN passed validation. Infinity and bool likewise slipped through the hypotheses map, which was never checked value-by-value.

2_duplicate_json_keys.now: strict_loads rejects duplicate keys at EVERY level via object_pairs_hook, and rejects NaN/Infinity literals via parse_constant. Wired into both adapters.
2_duplicate_json_keys.was: json.loads keeps the LAST value on a duplicate key, so {"H07": 0.2, "H07": 1.0} collapsed to a perfectly valid single-hypothesis commitment. Preserving the raw proposal documented the event but did not stop the parsed deposit from driving the session — so 'no semantic repair' did not fully hold.

3_one_IG_meaning.now: the guard lives in the primitive: repeated EXPERIMENT and re-PROBE of a fully known vector both return zero. Verified equal to the corrected version on all actions.
3_one_IG_meaning.was: world_b1.information_gain mispriced a repeated EXPERIMENT on an already-tested symbol (apply_action overwrites the outcome, fabricating a counterfactual branch that breaks sum p_out = 1), while ig_state.information_gain_full guarded it. Two functions, two answers, and the scripted learner plus probe-quality used the unguarded one.

4_incompleteness_semantics.now: a fourth runtime verdict UNGUARANTEED_INCOMPLETENESS, computed from D_lower(belief), matching A-008 exactly and carrying scored=false.
4_incompleteness_semantics.was: the session asked only whether success was GUARANTEED, so it labelled the middle band CORRECT_INCOMPLETENESS while A-008 does not score that band at all — provenance and scientific endpoint disagreeing about the same decision point.

5_R001_scoring.now: the prediction and the death boundary are reported separately and the Brier scores the PREDICTION. The variance clause is explicitly recorded as NEVER OPERATIONALIZED in the pre-registration (no estimator, no threshold): it is not computed and cannot flip the verdict, because defining it now would be a post-hoc definition needing its own amendment. Verdict unchanged (8/10 meets the real threshold); Brier 0.0417 now derives from the correct booleans.
5_R001_scoring.principle: forecast target != falsification boundary; a death boundary must never be silently promoted to held=True.
5_R001_scoring.was: F1 was implemented as (n_solved >= 6), which is the DEATH BOUNDARY, not the sealed prediction (>= 8/10). A run at 6/10 would have been recorded as HELD and fed into the Brier. The sealed variance clause was never computed at all.

fixes.6_exact_schema: unknown fields are now rejected for every deposit type and inside blind entries, matching the contract's claim of an exact structure.
fixes.7_append_concurrency: the archivist takes an exclusive file lock and fsyncs before releasing. Recorded limit: this guards the write, not the read-then-write race, so one chain file still belongs to one process; the lock is a last-resort guard, not a licence for parallel runs.

minor: n_paid renamed to n_actions in the efficiency audit (it counts free observations too)
compare_efficiency_vs_undersampling carried a superseded reading of the failures and now points at the action-space finding instead
the B1 adapter resets its raw buffer before each request so a failed call cannot leave the previous response in place
payload.past_results: NOT invalidated. The two contract bugs are latent vulnerabilities and there is no evidence they were exercised in 4000-4029; the IG discrepancy only affects repeated actions, which the traces did not contain, and the audit matched the recorded values. What changes is that the implementation can now be called airtight on these axes, which it could not before.
payload.status: sealed after review; both suites re-run before any further confirmatory work
payload.title: Contract hardening after external code review: finite probabilities, strict JSON, exact fields, one IG meaning, aligned incompleteness semantics
payload.trigger: external review of the code on main found two contract bugs, two semantic inconsistencies and one confirmatory-scoring error. None invalidate past results, but 'no evidence the past results are wrong' is not 'the implementation is airtight'.
payload.triple_freeze_correction: the validator was tightened while schema_hash stayed identical, which contradicts the project's own doctrine that a change of MEANING requires a new version even when the JSON shape is unchanged. The strictness is now part of COMMIT_SCHEMA, so the hash moves with the semantics.
